title: M5 — Auditable agent (session logging)
source: SPECIFICATION.md §6 (agent wrapper), §7 (harness), §11 (M5 milestone), §12 (session_driver + harness_driver). Milestone M5: M4 plus session logging. Every event the agent emits is durable to disk in the JSONL tree format. Adds the agent wrapper (subscription fan-out, single-flight, observable state), the session writer, entry ID generation, and the assembled harness. Introduces session_driver and harness_driver.

baseline.notes:
M4 (acting agent) is complete. Libraries: pera_types, pera_provider, pera_core, pera_core_test_util, pera_harness, pera_tools. Drivers: provider_driver, loop_driver, conversation_driver, env_driver, tool_driver.

DESIGN DECISIONS settled (do not revisit without asking):
(1) PACKAGE SPLIT: Execution_env+Local_env move to new pera_env package. pera_tools depends on pera_env (not pera_harness). Agent_harness lives in new pera_agent package depending on pera_harness+pera_tools. No cycles. Stage 0 includes this restructure.
(2) pera_harness gains pera_core, pera_provider, yojson, uuidm deps. Acceptable: heavyweight components belong in implementation packages.
(3) Entry IDs: Standard non-truncated UUIDv7 strings (full 36-character representation) via Uuidm.v7_non_monotonic_gen. The full representation guarantees uniqueness, so there is NO allocation-time collision check and NO seen_ids table. Reliable lexicographical time-ordering from the UUIDv7 timestamp prefix. Clock non-monotonicity within a millisecond is not a practical concern; document at the generator. (Diverges from old SPEC '8-char truncated'; SPECIFICATION.md §3 updated to match.)
(4) Session_writer uses Eio.Path.with_open_out ~append:true per entry + Eio.File.sync. Re-opens per entry. Fine at turn-boundary rates.
(5) All session writes from event subscriber. Disk failure handling deferred.
(6) User messages written by Agent_harness.send before Agent_loop.run.
(7) ACTOR/MAILBOX: Agent_wrapper.create ~sw forks a long-lived actor fibre. send enqueues Run{messages; reply: Promise.u} to a capacity-1 Eio.Stream, then awaits the reply promise. Actor processes one run at a time; uses Fun.protect to always resolve reply (including on exception/cancellation). send has NO ~sw parameter. Agent_harness.create gains ~sw; Agent_harness.send drops ~sw.
(8) Leaf semantics (childless, per-run): a Leaf entry is a childless marker. Session_writer.write_leaf appends a Leaf parented at the current tip but does NOT advance current_parent_id — only write_leaf is non-advancing; all other writers advance. Exactly one Leaf is written per run at AE_agent_end (NOT per turn at AE_turn_end). Content entries always chain off the previous content entry, never off a Leaf. Restore walks back from the most recent Leaf. See SPECIFICATION.md §3 'Two senses of leaf'.
(9) convert_to_llm uses refutation syntax `| Synthetic _ -> .` (synthetic is already `type synthetic = |` in Pera_core.Agent_types; no modification to Agent_types needed).
(10) Prompt_assembly inlined in Agent_harness.
(11) cost_usd type: Pera_types.Types.usage.cost_usd changes from `float option` to `Decimal.t option` using the ocaml-decimal opam package (library 'decimal', module Decimal; https://github.com/yawaramin/ocaml-decimal). This is a cross-cutting pera_types change; Stage 0 Part F enumerates every construction/match site that must be touched and the dune files that gain the `decimal` dep. Serialised to JSON as a string (Decimal.to_string) when Some, key omitted when None.
(12) HTTP connect_timeout is unrelated to M5 and is isolated in its own stage (Epoch 4, Stage 7); it is not a dependency of any M5 stage.
(13) EXEC_ENV INJECTION: Agent_harness.config gains exec_env: (module Pera_env.Execution_env.S). Agent_harness.create no longer constructs Local_env internally; the caller is responsible for supplying the execution environment. This enables Sandboxed_env or any other Execution_env.S implementation to be injected without modifying Agent_harness. ~env:Eio_unix.Stdenv.base is retained in create for Session_writer's Eio.Path filesystem access. pera_tools already accepts (module Execution_env.S) polymorphically and needs no change.

PACKAGE DEPENDENCY GRAPH AFTER M5:
pera_types <- pera_provider <- pera_core <- pera_core_test_util
pera_types <- pera_env <- pera_harness
pera_core <- pera_harness
pera_env <- pera_tools
pera_core <- pera_tools
pera_harness + pera_tools <- pera_agent

REUSE AUDIT:
- Execution_env.S, Local_env: MOVE to pera_env (Stage 0).
- Tools.default, etc: pera_tools dep changes from pera_harness to pera_env.
- Agent_loop.run, Agent_types: REUSE from pera_core.
- Faux_provider.stream_fn_of_scripts: REUSE from pera_core_test_util.

NEW MODULES:
- pera_env package: Execution_env, Local_env (moved from pera_harness).
- Entry_id (pera_harness): UUIDv7 ID generation.
- Session_types (pera_harness): entry type defs + JSON codec.
- Session_writer (pera_harness): JSONL writer with fsync.
- Agent_wrapper (pera_harness): actor/mailbox wrapper over Agent_loop.run.
- pera_agent package: Agent_harness (assembled harness).
- session_driver, harness_driver (bin/drivers).

KEY RISKS:
- Eio.File.sync type compatibility with with_open_out callback arg. Fallback: open_out ~sw + explicit close.
- Synthetic refutation pattern: verify with dune build at Stage 4.
- Actor reply promise unresolved if actor fibre dies: Fun.protect in actor loop handles this.

PART E — Entry_id module (full UUIDv7, no truncation, no dedup):
entry_id.mli:
  type t = string
  val generate : unit -> t
  (* generate () returns a fresh standard 36-character UUIDv7 string. *)
entry_id.ml:
  let rand_state = Random.State.make_self_init ()
  let gen = Uuidm.v7_non_monotonic_gen ~now_ms:(fun () -> Int64.of_float (Unix.gettimeofday () *. 1000.)) rand_state
  let generate () = Uuidm.to_string (gen ())
NOTE: full 36-char representation guarantees uniqueness, so there is NO seen_ids table and NO collision/dedup loop. Add a code comment that clock non-monotonicity within a millisecond is acceptable for session ordering.

Construction/match sites to update (set cost_usd = None unchanged-in-shape, or wrap real values in Decimal.of_string / Decimal.of_float):

Most sites set cost_usd = None and only need the dune dep if they pattern-match the field's type; sites that build a numeric cost must use Decimal. Verify equal_usage / pp_usage / show_usage still derive (ppx_deriving over Decimal.t needs Decimal to provide equal/pp, or write them manually — confirm at build; if ppx_deriving.eq/show cannot derive over Decimal.t, hand-write equal_usage/pp_usage or wrap with a custom comparator).

stages.title: Session_writer — JSONL + fsync
stages.description: Append-only JSONL session file writer. Manages the current_parent_id chain internally. Each append_entry call writes one JSON line + newline then calls Eio.File.sync before returning. Uses Eio.Path.with_open_out per entry. write_leaf appends a childless Leaf marker WITHOUT advancing the tip (per SPECIFICATION.md §3); all other writers advance current_parent_id.
stages.implementation_notes:
INTERFACE:
type t
val create : path:string -> env:Eio_unix.Stdenv.base -> model:Pera_types.Types.model -> cwd:string -> (t, Pera_types.Types.file_error) result
val write_session_info : t -> (unit, Pera_types.Types.file_error) result
val write_message : t -> Pera_provider.Provider.message -> (unit, Pera_types.Types.file_error) result
val write_leaf : t -> (unit, Pera_types.Types.file_error) result
val write_model_change : t -> Pera_types.Types.model -> (unit, Pera_types.Types.file_error) result
val session_id : t -> string
val current_parent_id : t -> Entry_id.t option

INTERNAL STATE:
type t = {
  path: string;
  base: Eio.Fs.dir_ty Eio.Path.t;  (* env#fs stored at create time *)
  session_id: string;
  model: Pera_types.Types.model;
  cwd: string;
  mutable current_parent_id: Entry_id.t option;
}

APPEND_LINE:
let append_line t json =
  catch_write t.path (fun () ->
    let line = Yojson.Safe.to_string json ^ "\n" in
    Eio.Path.with_open_out ~append:true ~create:(`If_missing 0o644)
      Eio.Path.(t.base / t.path)
      (fun file ->
        Eio.Flow.copy_string line file;
        Eio.File.sync file))

EIO API NOTES:
- Eio.Path.with_open_out : ?append:bool -> create:create -> _ t -> (File.rw_ty r -> 'a) -> 'a  (no ~sw)
- Eio.Flow.copy_string : string -> _ #Flow.sink -> unit  (file satisfies #Flow.sink via rw_ty includes Flow.sink_ty)
- Eio.File.sync : _ rw -> unit  (file satisfies _ rw via File.rw_ty)
- If type errors at compile time, use: Eio.Path.open_out ~sw ~append:true ~create:(`If_missing 0o644) path, then Eio.Flow.copy_string; Eio.File.sync; Eio.Resource.close. Requires sw threaded through.

CREATE - directory creation:
let parent = Filename.dirname path in
(try Eio.Path.mkdirs ~exists_ok:true ~perm:0o755 Eio.Path.(base / parent)
 with _ -> ());
Note: mkdirs may raise on permission errors; catch those in the outer result.

write_session_info allocates entry_id, builds SessionInfo entry, calls append_line, sets current_parent_id.
write_message allocates entry_id, builds Message entry with parent=current_parent_id, calls append_line, updates current_parent_id.
write_model_change: same advancing pattern for ModelChange entry.
write_leaf: allocates entry_id, builds Leaf entry with parent=current_parent_id, calls append_line, but does NOT update current_parent_id. The Leaf is a childless marker; the tip stays at the last content entry so the next content entry parents to that entry, not to the Leaf. write_leaf is the ONLY non-advancing writer.

Error handling: catch_write wraps Eio.Io exceptions to file_error codes (same pattern as local_env.ml). Return (unit, file_error) result from all write functions.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: pera-specific.md — IO functions return Result, never raise
eio.md — no ~sw stored in writer struct; sync via Eio.File.sync not Unix.fsync
error-handling.md — use Result.Syntax bind operators for chains
nesting-and-control-flow.md — max 2 levels of nesting in write functions

stages.title: Agent_wrapper — actor/mailbox + subscription + observable state
stages.description: Actor-pattern wrapper over Agent_loop.run. create ~sw forks a long-lived actor fibre under the wrapper's switch. send enqueues a Run message to a capacity-1 mailbox (Eio.Stream) and awaits a reply promise. Actor processes runs sequentially; Fun.protect ensures the reply promise is always resolved. Provides subscription fan-out and observable state.

pera-specific.md — open Containers; mutable state updates sequenced by cooperative scheduling

stages.title: session_driver
stages.description: Layer driver for Session_writer. Appends representative entry sequences and verifies the JSONL output structure. Does not involve the agent loop or Faux_provider. Five scenarios covering the full entry-type vocabulary.
stages.implementation_notes:
DUNE STANZA:
(executable
 (name session_driver)
 (libraries pera_harness pera_provider pera_types eio eio_main eio_linux
            containers yojson))

SCENARIOS (5):
1. header_then_leaf: SessionInfo + Leaf. Verify: 2 lines; Leaf parent_id = SessionInfo id.
2. user_assistant_turn: SessionInfo + UserMessage + AssistantMessage + Leaf. Verify: 4 lines; types in order; parent chain linear.
3. tool_use_turn: SessionInfo + UserMessage + AssistantMessage + ToolResultMessage + Leaf. Verify: 5 lines; all types present.
4. two_turns (childless-leaf chain): SessionInfo + UserMsg1 + AssistantMsg1 + Leaf1 + UserMsg2 + AssistantMsg2 + Leaf2. Verify: 7 lines; UserMsg2 parent_id = AssistantMsg1 id (NOT Leaf1 id — proves write_leaf is non-advancing); Leaf2 parent_id = AssistantMsg2 id; no entry has a Leaf id as its parent_id.
5. model_change: SessionInfo + ModelChange + UserMessage + AssistantMessage + Leaf. Verify: ModelChange entry has correct model.id; UserMessage parent_id = ModelChange id (model_change advances the tip).

HELPERS:

stages.title: harness_driver
stages.description: Layer driver for Agent_harness. Exercises the full stack (session writer + agent wrapper + tools) against Faux_provider. Three scenarios verifying that the session log reflects the events and the parent chain is well-formed.
stages.implementation_notes:
DUNE STANZA:
(executable
 (name harness_driver)
 (libraries pera_agent pera_tools pera_harness pera_core pera_core_test_util pera_provider
            pera_types eio eio_main eio_linux containers yojson))

SCENARIOS (3):

1. text_only:
   Script: 1-turn Faux (text reply, EndTurn).
   Inject stream_fn = Faux_provider.stream_fn_of_scripts [Turn{events=[AME_text_delta{text="Hello",partial=...}; AME_done{message=...}]; final=...}].
   send "What is 2+2?".
   Verify: session file has 4 entries; types = [session_info; message(user); message(assistant); leaf]; parent chain linear.

2. tool_use:
   Script: 2-turn Faux. Turn 1: tool call (ToolUse stop). Turn 2: text reply (EndTurn).
   Provide a tool named 'echo' with mode=Parallel, execute returns Tool_text of its 'text' arg.
   Pass tool as part of the harness config tools.
   Actually: Agent_harness creates tools via Tools.default env. The faux script must produce a tool call whose name matches one of read/write/bash/grep. Easiest: script a 'read' tool call with path='/dev/null' - it will actually execute.
   Alternative: use a simpler approach - script the turn to have EndTurn (no tool calls) and verify 4 entries. Then in turn 2 scenario, script a ToolUse turn + text turn. The harness uses real tools (Local_env). The bash tool can echo something simple.
   Recommended: script tool_use scenario as: bash tool call 'echo hello'. The harness_driver creates a Local_env with a temp cwd (Pera_env.Local_env.create ~env ~cwd) and passes it as config.exec_env. The bash tool executes and produces a result. Verify 6 entries (ONE leaf per send, at AE_agent_end — not per turn): session_info + user + assistant(ToolUse) + tool_result + assistant(EndTurn) + leaf. Check the content chain excludes the leaf and is gap-free; the leaf is childless.

3. subscriber_events:
   Text-only scenario. Subscribe to collect events. Verify events include AE_agent_start, AE_turn_start, AE_message_start, AE_message_end, AE_turn_end, AE_agent_end in order.

HELPERS:
parse_session_file: same as session_driver.
check_content_chain + assert_leaves_childless: same as session_driver (chain excludes 'leaf' entries; leaves must be childless).
get_type_field json: Yojson.Safe.Util.(member "type" json |> to_string).
make_temp_dir env: same as tool_driver.

For Faux_provider events: build minimal assistant_message values (same pattern as loop_driver.make_assistant_message).

PRINT: '[harness] <scenario_name> ... PASS/FAIL: <reason>'
EXIT: 0 if all pass, 1 otherwise.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: test-patterns.md — driver exercises public interface; if driver is hard to write, seam is leaking
eio.md — all IO under Eio_main.run and Eio.Switch.run

test_requirements.notes:
Drivers are not Alcotest tests. Expected output:
[harness] text_only ... PASS
[harness] tool_use ... PASS
[harness] subscriber_events ... PASS
The tool_use scenario requires the bash tool to actually execute (real Local_env). Ensure the temp dir is writable and /bin/sh is available.

tool_use: session file includes tool_result message entry
subscriber_events: collected events include AE_agent_start and AE_agent_end
All scenarios print PASS, exit 0
